messages:
anya: quick question  should manifest negotiation and provenance live in the weightsource/proxy or inside the runtime loader? i'm leaning proxy for centralization.
marco: proxy for negotiation + signing makes rollout easier. runtimes just consume a canonical blob map.
sophia: +1, but we need an explicit provenance chain (who signed what, which tool emitted the pack). otherwise auditing is messy.
lee: runtime still needs some levers. e.g. decide fast vs thorough validation. suggest a tiny capability field on the manifest request like `capabilities=hotstart,stream`.
sam: can we design manifest-v2 with a compact hotstart hint? eg `hot_windows` as array of byte ranges per shard to prioritize. also add `eviction_group` tag so scheduler can co-locate/migrate safely.
anya: draft example of manifest-v2 response: 
```
GET /v2/manifest?model=foo&ver=2026-03&capabilities=hotstart,stream
200 OK
{
  "format": "safetensors+split",
  "blobs": ["s3://models/foo/part-000","s3://models/foo/part-001"],
  "checksums": ["sha256:aaa...","sha256:bbb..."],
  "provenance": ["sign:v1:sig...","tool:bundle-gen@2026-03-18"],
  "hot_windows": [[0,131072],[0,65536]],
  "eviction_group": "g-ml-71",
  "fallback_endpoints": ["https://stream-proxy.internal/models/foo/stream"],
  "compat_flags": ["lazy-warmstart"]
}
```
marco: that looks good. note `provenance` needs to be a signed Merkle header ideally, but we can start with simple signatures and a tool chain stamp.
sophia: security: runtime should enforce allowed signature schemes (ed25519/ecdsa) and refuse manifests signed with weak algos. weightsource should advertise `sig_algo` in the response.
lee: validation strategy: runtime does a small async pre-validate: fetch first 4KB of each blob, validate checksum prefix, then mmap. avoids mmap'ing silently corrupted files.
sam: fallback policy: if proxy provides `fallback_endpoints`, runtime can choose streaming adapter when cold-start budget is tight. we should expose `?gating=fast-warmup` so caller can indicate preference.
anya: error taxonomy suggestion: 4xx=manifest/compat (don't retry), 409=version-mismatch (client should refresh), 5xx=transient transport (retry/backoff). warmup coordinator uses this.
marco: rollout plan: implement a lightweight translation layer in weight-proxy that emits manifest-v2 from existing metadata. allow runtimes to opt-in via header `Accept: application/vnd.redwood.manifest-v2+json`.
sophia: operational note: add `eviction_group` into metrics so load tests can detect cross-group thrashing.
ci-bot: perf note: canary with proxy negotiation saved ~0.9ms median model-load vs runtime negotiation. streaming fallback + fast gating reduced 95p cold-start by ~120ms in last run.
lee: one more thing: add `canonical_order` field in manifest to avoid nondeterministic shard ordering across sources. critical for deterministic checksums and streaming offsets.
anya: action items: marco + sophia to spec proto + sig handling; lee to draft runtime pre-validate and gating semantics; sam to wire eviction_group into warmup scheduler; i'll file follow-up RFC and link this thread.
marco: ack  will start translation shim PR.
sophia: ack  will list accepted sig algos and fallback behaviour.
ci-bot: reminder  tag RFC PR with `eng-ml/warmup` and include perf trace logs.
